notes: Intro call 2026-02-25 w/ CTO (Marta Silva) + Infra lead (Owen Park). High-level interest in Dedicated for latency predictability.
Primary ask: guaranteed throughput for live-chat: target 400–600 requests/sec (avg payload ~320 tokens) with p95 latency <= 200ms for generation endpoint.

Reserved GPU planning: Valley of ops wants initial reservation = 8 rtx-h100-equivalent GPUs (estimate), tiered burst to shared capacity during peak. Asking for guidance on mapping to Redwood Dedicated node counts.

Autoscaling policy requirements discussed: scale-up aggressive (add nodes when queue_depth > 40 for 20s), scale-down conservative (idle 10m before decommission), warm-pool min nodes = 2 per availability zone.
Queueing behavior: prefer client-side retry + server queue with priority for webchat traffic; need per-route queue thresholds and per-customer QoS bands. Wants backlog visibility in Console.
Warm pools: require pre-warmed KV cache and warmed model weights to avoid cold-start latency; ask for standard warm-pool warmup time and recommended pool sizes per model family.
SLA negotiation points: uptime target 99.95% for Dedicated, latency SLOs with p95 and p99 bands, financial credits on SLA breach. Legal asked for sample SLA clause (sent request: drive doc).
Security & compliance: strict VPC peering, customer KMS for encryption at rest, audit logs retention 365 days, SSO via SAML, SOC2 attestation required.
Cost sensitivity: willing to commit to reserved capacity for 12–24 months in exchange for reduced unit pricing; needs clear modeling of committed vs burst costs.

Model routing: primary preference for open Llama-2-70B optimized variant; fallback to quantized 13B variant for cost-critical bursts. Want automatic fallback routing policy and graceful degradation rules.
Quote from Owen Park: "We care less about absolute throughput numbers than predictable tail latency during business hours — outages are very expensive."
Requested benchmarks: p95/p99 latency under 3 concurrent traffic profiles (steady 500rps, spike 2k rps for 2 minutes, evening taper) and warm/cold-start curves for scaling events.
Requested artifacts: network diagram, firewall rules, certificate requirements (sent by infra), Redwood asked for a test token for POC staging VPC peering.
Next: POC kickoff 2026-03-15. SE to deliver config template: node sizing, autoscale rules, warm-pool config, queue thresholds, health-checks, and test scenarios.
Decision criteria: meets latency SLOs for primary chat workflow; autoscale ramps without >10% request loss; economic model within forecast ARR band.
Internal note: legal flagged standardized indemnity language; procurement wants 60-day payment terms — potential negotiation point.
